verdict_reason: Step A of six implemented and verified; steps B-F (WorkerManager child resume, durable resume actions, write API, Dash controls, write E2E) not implemented. The section 16 acceptance gate requires all of them.

direct_path_characterization.method: identical batch sequence via DataLoader(shuffle=False) vs BatchPlan(shuffle=False)
direct_path_characterization.shuffled_difference_cause: DataLoader.__iter__ draws a random_() for its worker base seed, and RandomSampler evaluates and discards a trailing randperm each epoch; reproducing that would pin the batch plan to torch sampler internals
direct_path_characterization.conclusion: the loops are semantically equivalent; only batch-order derivation differs, so the two paths are separated in structural provenance rather than declared interchangeable

security_boundary.note: read-only remains intact trivially, because no write surface was added

remaining_risks: five of six tranche steps are unimplemented (B-F)
training_path_id is not yet propagated to the registry run row, checkpoint manifest, or API/UI, which ADR-WC-004 requires and which capability gating for the write API depends on

_call_resumable_train is unit-tested for dispatch and refusal-to-fall-back but has not been exercised end-to-end through a real certified suite run, so its dataset-split and batch_size plumbing is unproven
shuffled legacy and shuffled control runs are not numerically comparable; enforced by differing structural hashes and documented, but relevant to anyone aggregating historical results
BatchPlan.shuffle changes plan_id inputs; no production checkpoint predates it, but a plan stored before this commit would hash differently
recommended_next_step: propagate training_path_id into the registry row and checkpoint manifest, then implement WorkerManager child launch, since the write API and Dash controls both depend on it
